---
title: "Rotations on the Coordinate Plane"
subtitle: "An interactive high-school geometry lesson"
---

In this lesson, you will build a convex polygon on a coordinate grid, choose its center of rotation, and explore how each vertex moves as you adjust the angle from −360° to 360°.

## Interactive rotation tool

Click grid intersections to add vertices of a convex polygon. After the third point, the tool arranges accepted vertices around the boundary automatically. Duplicate points and points inside the boundary are not added. Choose the rotation center on the grid or enter its coordinates.

```{=html}

  <fieldset class="rotation-center-controls">
    <legend>Center of rotation</legend>
    <label for="center-x">x</label>
    <input id="center-x" type="number" min="-8" max="8" step="1" value="0">

      <table class="rotation-distance-table">

      <th scope="col">Image: to x-axis</th>
    </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody id="rotation-distance-values"></tbody>
</table>
    </div>
    <p class="rotation-distance-note">With the center at the origin, 90° and 270° rotations swap the x- and y-distances, while a 180° rotation keeps them on their respective axes. If the center is elsewhere, distances to the coordinate axes are not generally preserved.</p>
  </section>

  <label class="rotation-distance-toggle" for="show-local-axes">
    <input id="show-local-axes" type="checkbox">
    Show x̂ and ŷ axes through the center
  </label>

  <label class="rotation-distance-toggle" for="show-local-distances">

  <section id="rotation-local-distance-panel" class="rotation-distance-panel" hidden aria-labelledby="rotation-local-distance-title">
```

## What to notice

A rotation turns every point through the same angle about a fixed center. In this tool, you choose the center $(h,k)$. Each vertex stays the same distance from that center, and the polygon keeps its side lengths and angle measures.

For a counterclockwise rotation by θ degrees around $(h,k)$, transform each point using:

**x′ = h + (x − h) cos θ − (y − k) sin θ**\
**y′ = k + (x − h) sin θ + (y − k) cos θ**

## Explore

1.  Plot a triangle, then rotate it by 90°. Compare the original and image coordinates. What pattern do you notice?
2.  Try 180°, −90°, and 270°. Which rotations produce the same image? Explain why.
3.  Rotate your polygon by 360° and −360°. What happens to each vertex?
4.  Predict the image of one vertex before moving the slider, then use the graph to check your prediction.

## Learning goals

- Plot and identify vertices of a polygon on the coordinate plane.
- Describe and model a rotation by its angle and center.
- Compare coordinates before and after a rotation and explain how the transformation preserves distance and angle measure.
